## Target context

- Env: dev
- Project: (none)

[F007] I implemented F007's future-command guidance gate. **Side-effect commands run:** none — only local file edits and read-only pytest invocations (no cloud/CLI mutations).

I added two pure helpers to `command_guidance.py` — `missing_guidance_commands()` (names any validator-vocabulary command lacking a class/example entry instead of a deep `KeyError`) and a `WORKFLOW_CRITICAL_HELP_COMMANDS` constant (the one-per-class help surfaces that must carry the agent-guidance footer) — both exported via `__all__`. The new test suite `test_f007_command_guidance_gate.py` (15 tests) covers all four AC mechanisms: AC1 asserts zero missing-guidance commands today *and* proves the gate actually fires by monkeypatching a fake `frobnicate` command into the validator vocabulary (helper reports it, inventory build raises); AC2 renders each workflow-critical `--help` and asserts its shared snippet is present, plus parity between the constant and the help-argv map and full command-class coverage; AC3 validates every surfaced guidance example (and a narrowed automatable-class pass) against `command_validation.validate_command_tokens`; AC4 asserts the new `docs/AGENT_COMMAND_GUIDANCE_CHECKLIST.md` exists and is anchored to the real source tables. All targeted suites pass — 133 across the F007 gate, the F001 command-validation suite, the F005 representative-help suite, and the F002 guidance suite (AC5), and the adjacent F003/F004/F006 suites stay green (33 more).
